SEO.DEFAULT_DESCRIPTION: Mapping artists from Eastern Europe and Austria who migrated to Brazil, 1918–1989, based on the MAC USP collection.

COLLECTION.TITLE: Trajectories of artists from <hl>Eastern Europe and Austria</hl> in Brazil
COLLECTION.BODY: An atlas built from the MAC USP collection: works, exhibitions and publications linked to the places and dates of each artist's trajectory.

PROBLEM.TITLE: Digitisation widened access, but not the <hl>intelligibility</hl> of collections
PROBLEM.BODY: Works, exhibitions and publications sit in separate records. The Atlas brings them together in each artist's record, with the source of every piece of information.

RELATIONS.TITLE: From static cataloguing to a <hl>dynamic logic of relations</hl>
RELATIONS.BODY: The network links artists, works, exhibitions, publications, institutions and places; the historical layer shows the borders of each period.

AI.TITLE: AI as an <hl>assistive and exploratory</hl> tool, with critical mediation
AI.BODY: Relational AI searches open sources and shows each finding with its source, its reliability and the prompt used: verifiable, auditable hypotheses.

COUNTERS.TITLE: The collection in numbers
COUNTERS.UNAVAILABLE: The collection figures could not be loaded right now.

NEED.TITLE: A collection read in relation
NEED.CONTEXT: Between 1918 and 1989, artists born in Eastern Europe and Austria migrated to Brazil. Their works are in the MAC USP collection, but the museum's records do not show, on their own, where these artists came from, where they went and whom they were connected to.
NEED.PROBLEM: The Atlas brings these records together and reads them in relation: on the map, in time, within the borders of each period and in a network of links, always with the source of each piece of information and without filling in what the source does not give.

IMPACTS.TITLE: What changes for research and for the collection

ITEMS.1: The artists' trajectories gathered on one map, filtered by country of origin and period.
ITEMS.2: Relations between artists, works, exhibitions and publications that were scattered across separate records.
ITEMS.3: Findings from open sources with their source, reliability and prompt in view, ready to be checked.

ITEMS.1: The MAC USP records gain geographical and historical context, with the borders of each period.
ITEMS.2: Every piece of information keeps its provenance, and what is inferred stays apart from what is documented.
ITEMS.3: Gaps stay visible: what the source does not give shows as unknown and is never filled in.

HISTORICAL_LAYER.TITLE: Historical Layer
HISTORICAL_LAYER.INTRO: Europe with each year's borders, to read every artist's place of origin in the state that existed at the time, including states that later ceased to exist, split or were renamed.
HISTORICAL_LAYER.DATA_UNAVAILABLE: The artists couldn't be loaded right now. Please try again shortly.
HISTORICAL_LAYER.BORDERS_UNAVAILABLE: The historical borders couldn't be loaded right now.
HISTORICAL_LAYER.MAP_LABEL: Map of Europe with the borders of {year}
HISTORICAL_LAYER.SOURCE_NOTE: Borders on 1 July of the chosen year, according to CShapes 2.0. The dataset follows Gleditsch and Ward's list of states: states occupied or annexed in the Second World War, such as Poland and Austria, keep their borders, and territories that belonged to no state on that day have no border. Each state bears the name it had on that day (Russian Empire until 1917, Soviet Russia until 1922 and Soviet Union after; Austria-Hungary until 1918), and those annexed or partitioned in the war say so.
HISTORICAL_LAYER.ORIGINS_METHOD: Each place's state was derived from its position inside the borders of the time. When the birth date is only a year and the border moved during that year, both states are shown.
HISTORICAL_LAYER.BORN_HERE: {count, plural, =0 {No artist was born in places that belonged to this state in {year}.} one {# artist was born in a place that belonged to this state in {year}:} other {# artists were born in places that belonged to this state in {year}:}}

STATE.UNKNOWN: undetermined (unknown date or outside the dataset, which covers 1886–2019)
STATE.CHANGED: {from} or {to}: the border moved in this period

HISTORICAL_LAYER.CREDIT: Borders: CShapes 2.0 by Schvitz, Rüegger, Girardin, Cederman, Weidmann and Gleditsch (ETH Zürich, 2022), CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 license. Clipped and simplified for Europe by the Atlas.

RESEARCH.TITLE: Relational AI
RESEARCH.INTRO: Links each artist in the collection to what open sources say about them. Every finding shows the page it came from and how reliable it is, and nothing found here enters the base without review.
RESEARCH.PICK_HINT: Choose an artist to search the open sources.
RESEARCH.LIST_UNAVAILABLE: The list of artists could not be loaded right now. Please try again shortly.
RESEARCH.UNAVAILABLE: The open-source search is not available right now. Please try again shortly.
RESEARCH.NOT_FOUND: This artist is not in the collection.

BASIS.BIRTH_YEAR: Chosen as the only person with this name born in the year the collection records.
BASIS.NAME: The collection has no birth year; chosen as the only person with exactly this name.

RESEARCH.NO_FINDINGS: The person found has none of this information on Wikidata.
RESEARCH.REFERENCES: {count, plural, =0 {no references} one {# reference} other {# references}}

REVIEW.PRESENT_DAY_NAME: Review: the source uses the present-day name of the place or state, not the period's.
REVIEW.CONFLICTS_WITH_COLLECTION: Review: the date differs from the one in the collection.

RESEARCH.QUERY_TEXT: Searches Wikidata for the name “{name}”; of the people found, only the one that is certainly this artist is kept. From it the search reads the dates and places of birth and death, citizenship, occupation, movement, education, institutions they were a member of and notable works, and the lead of the Wikipedia article in Portuguese (or English, when there is none).
RESEARCH.METHOD_RELIABILITY: A finding is documented when Wikidata cites references for it; with no references, or when it comes from encyclopedia text, it is undetermined.
RESEARCH.METHOD_PERIOD: Open sources use the present-day names of places and states. The AI is given the states of the birth year and told to use the names of the time.
RESEARCH.METHOD_AI: The summary is written by Gemini at a low temperature, only from the numbered findings, the collection's record and the period's map. A summary that cites no finding, or one that does not exist, is discarded.
RESEARCH.AI_NOTE: Written by AI ({model}) only from the numbered findings and the collection's record, within the period's geopolitics. Each number leads to the finding the claim comes from; check the source before using it.

AI_STATUS.NOT_CONFIGURED: The AI summary is not active in this environment. The prompt that would be sent is under “How the search works”.
AI_STATUS.REJECTED: The AI wrote a summary that did not cite the findings correctly, so it is not shown.
AI_STATUS.ERROR: The AI did not answer just now. The findings still stand; please try again shortly.

RESEARCH.PERIOD_APPROXIMATE: The birth year is approximate in the collection.
RESEARCH.PERIOD_STATES: {count, plural, one {# state in Europe that day} other {# states in Europe that day}}
RESEARCH.PERIOD_SOURCE: CShapes 2.0 borders, read on 1 July of the birth year, as on the Historical Layer. This is the map the AI is given.
RESEARCH.PERIOD_UNAVAILABLE: The birth year is unknown or outside the period the borders cover, so the AI is not given the period's map.

OVERVIEW.TITLE: AI research on this artist
OVERVIEW.FOUND: Information found by the automated research of {date} on {platforms}. Each finding below links to the page it came from.
OVERVIEW.NOT_FOUND: No concrete data on this artist was found by the research on {platforms} on {date}.
OVERVIEW.PENDING: Research pending: Wikidata did not answer in the research of {date}, so it is not yet known whether there is data on this artist.
OVERVIEW.NONE_FOUND: Nobody with this name was found on Wikidata. This is information for research to gather.
OVERVIEW.CANDIDATES_NOTE: None of them was linked automatically, so as not to give the artist someone else's life. If one is the artist, a researcher's confirmation lets it be linked.

REASON.BIRTH_YEAR_DIFFERS: Wikidata says born in {wikidata}; the collection, {collection}. Check which date is right.
REASON.NO_BIRTH_YEAR: Wikidata has no birth year, so it cannot be compared with the collection ({collection}).
REASON.AMBIGUOUS: More than one person on Wikidata fits the collection, so it is not possible to tell which is the artist.
REASON.SHORTER_NAME: Only turns up when searching “{foundBy}”, a name different from the collection's.
REASON.NAME_DIFFERS: The collection has no birth year, and the name on Wikidata is different.

ABOUT.TITLE: About the project
ABOUT.INTRO: Atlas Migrações Leste-Sul maps artists from Eastern Europe and Austria who migrated to Brazil between 1918 and 1989, based on the collection of the Museum of Contemporary Art of the University of São Paulo (MAC USP).

PROJECT.TITLE: The project
PROJECT.PROBLEM: Digitisation widened access to collections but did not make them intelligible.
PROJECT.QUESTION: How can AI help enrich, relate and interpret digitised art collections without losing historical and curatorial rigour?
PROJECT.GOAL: To develop an AI-based analytical framework to enrich and visualise historical relations in digitised collections.
PROJECT.HYPOTHESIS: AI systems, with critical and curatorial mediation, can reveal hidden connections and make collections more intelligible. AI is not treated as an automatic solution but as an assistive, exploratory tool to produce verifiable and auditable hypotheses.

METHOD.TITLE: Methodology
METHOD.READING_BODY: Defining the analytical scope, mapping and selecting data, ingesting and preparing the data for analysis.
METHOD.RELATION_BODY: Associating entities, recognising patterns, assessing relevance and discovering relations.
METHOD.RELIABILITY_BODY: Detecting inconsistencies, validating sources and flagging uncertainty.
METHOD.PROVENANCE: Every piece of information keeps its provenance, every inferred relation is distinguished from a documented one, and every hypothesis leads back to the sources it came from.

LEVELS.TITLE: Reading reliability
LEVELS.DOCUMENTED_BODY: Stated in an identified source, such as the MAC USP collection spreadsheets.
LEVELS.INFERRED_BODY: Derived by the platform from documented records, such as the trajectories drawn on the map.
LEVELS.UNDETERMINED_BODY: Not enough sources to confirm or deny it.

DATA.TITLE: Data
DATA.SOURCE: The base comes from three MAC USP collection spreadsheets of 16 July 2026: selected works, and the exhibitions and publications related to them.
DATA.PRECISION: Place names are kept as in the source, with the present-day name alongside when the source gives it. Dates show the precision the source gives (“c. 1949”, “1940–1945”, “n.d.”), and nothing missing from the source is filled in.
DATA.GAPS: The sources do not record the year of arrival or the route to Brazil, so the map draws a single line from the birthplace to the first documented place in Brazil, with no intermediate route. Exhibitions of the works during the artist's lifetime and the place of death appear as points.

CREDITS.TITLE: Cartography and credits
CREDITS.BASEMAP: Basemap: OpenFreeMap, with OpenStreetMap data (© OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL) in the OpenMapTiles schema. It shows only land and water, with no present-day borders or names.
CREDITS.HISTORICAL: Historical borders: CShapes 2.0 by Guy Schvitz, Seraina Rüegger, Luc Girardin, Lars-Erik Cederman, Nils Weidmann and Kristian Skrede Gleditsch (ETH Zürich; Journal of Conflict Resolution, 2022), CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 license. The Atlas clipped and simplified the borders for Europe, and the derived file keeps the same license.
CREDITS.SOFTWARE: Map rendered with MapLibre GL, free software.
CREDITS.COLLECTION: Collection data: Museum of Contemporary Art of the University of São Paulo (MAC USP).

TRAJECTORY.METHOD: The lines join, in date order, the points the collection documents: birth, exhibitions of the works during the artist's lifetime, and death. The stretch from the birthplace to the first documented place in Brazil is drawn in gold. The sources record neither the route nor the year of arrival, so the lines show the sequence of the records, not a documented journey.
TRAJECTORY.POSTHUMOUS: {count, plural, one {# posthumous exhibition is left out of the line.} other {# posthumous exhibitions are left out of the line.}}
TRAJECTORY.UNDRAWN: {count, plural, one {# point without a date or coordinates is left off the map.} other {# points without a date or coordinates are left off the map.}}
